title: [Fix] function-call: Preserve field names when removing schema identifiers
body:
## Motivation

Tool parameters can legitimately declare fields or definitions named `$id`, `$anchor`, or `$dynamicAnchor`. The recursive identifier filter currently removes those names from every dictionary, including `properties` and `$defs`. For example, a tool with `properties: {"$id": {"type": "mystery"}}` becomes an empty property map before `Draft202012Validator.check_schema`, so its invalid type is accepted. Referenced definitions and literal objects under `const`/`enum` are also altered.

This retains the legacy identifier compatibility introduced in #48343 while preserving the schema content being checked.

## Modifications

- Copy the input and use the existing schema-aware `_iter_subschemas` traversal.
- Remove identifier metadata only from schema nodes. Preserve map keys and instance-valued data.
- Extend the existing registered CPU test module with seven regression/control methods covering the native `Tool` → type normalization → schema-check path, definition references, schema maps, literal data, nested legacy identifiers, boolean schemas, and input immutability.

## Accuracy Tests

The existing test module passes: **30 test methods and 20 subtests**. Before the fix, four of the seven new methods exposed the defect: 15 failed subtests plus one failed method.

Test target:
`test/registered/unit/function_call/test_normalize_json_schema_types.py`

Validation used CPU Torch and the native SGLang protocol models, helper implementation, test classes, and jsonschema validators. The local launcher preloaded CPU Torch and scoped an empty, unused `triton` module with `unittest.mock.patch.dict`, following the unit-test README's external GPU import guidance, because the shared test utility imports Triton unconditionally. No Triton operation, GPU kernel, model inference, or HTTP server was executed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

This fixes tool-schema validation correctness. Inference throughput and model accuracy benchmarks are not applicable; no speed improvement is claimed.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and check the two changed files using the pinned applicable hook implementations directly: isort 7.0.0, Ruff 0.15.1, codespell 2.4.1, and pre-commit-hooks 6.0.0. The registered-test, package-test-placement, indirect-import, runtime-import, and pytest-entrypoint repository checks also pass. The full pre-commit environment installer was not run.
- [x] Add unit tests in the existing registered module using `CustomTestCase`.
- [x] Documentation assessed: the existing schema-check contract is restored; no new API or option is introduced.
- [x] Accuracy and speed applicability documented above.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from CODEOWNERS and other reviewers.
3. Trigger applicable CI tests or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.
